mu_name_from: MuPlayer.PartsForClass in the old client: the body a class wears with no armour equipped is HelmClass{NN}, ArmorClass{NN} and so on, and the numbering runs one over MU's zero-based classes - so Class01 is the Dark Wizard.
part_note: The head. Like the elf's it carries a ponytail bone the Dark Knight's has none of - six vertices on Bip01 Ponytail1 - and unlike either of theirs its seam is at Bip01 Neck rather than Bip01 Spine1: 63 vertices on the head against 7 on the neck. 114 triangles.
sheet_from: Data/Player/skin_barbarian_01.OZJ (256x256), from MuMain. All five parts name it.
sheet_warning: The sheet name is not the class, and this is the third of three that proves it: the Dark Wizard is painted on skin_barbarian_01, the Dark Knight on skin_wizard_01 and the Fairy Elf on skin_warrior_01. Not one of them matches. Verified by extracting each .bmd and reading the texture it names.
seam_note:
Not rebound, where HelmClass02 and HelmClass03 both are, and the difference is the bone rather than a change of mind. Those two split the head between Bip01 Head and Bip01 Spine1, which is two joints down: the head turns a long way from the chest in MU's poses, so a ring bound to the chest is wrung by the whole of that difference. This one splits between Head and *Neck*, one joint, where the difference is a fraction of it.

So the case for the fix is much weaker here and the fix is not free - it moves seven vertices onto a bone MU did not put them on. Left as MU bound it until somebody looks at this neck and says otherwise.
cull_from: As the other two heads: MU's hair is flat single-sided fins, and a culled fin does not turn away from the camera, it vanishes. See HelmClass02's cull_note for the whole argument and for the per-material answer that would settle it.
material_note:
Read off the sheet by cropping each island at its own mu_uv with V flipped. The Dark Wizard is the easiest of the three bodies to call, because almost all of him is one dark robe: the torso's large island is (120, 109, 101), the legs are (28, 28, 27) and (17, 17, 17), and the only flesh on him below the neck is two seven-triangle islands at (183, 153, 132) - the wrists, where the sleeve ends.

cloth for the robe, which is what the library has for hung, woven, never-taut fabric and is exactly what he is wearing. leather_wrap for the gloves at (41, 41, 41) and the boots at (55, 59, 58): darker than the robe, and worn hide rather than cloth. His hair samples (135, 146, 153), a grey-blue, which is the white hair MU gives him and not a lighting artefact.
unstack_why: Refuses the UV un-stacking, as ArmorClass01 does and for the reason found there: the step moved 69 of that part's 150 faces off their twin and the buckled vest vanished from the bake. Every part of this body is mirrored the same way - this one arrives 36.8% stacked and 33 of its faces get moved - so the same damage is available to all of them, and MU sharing one set of texels between a left and a right half is the arrangement rather than a defect to undo.
